theory_refs.at: For a fixed end, the best start comes from the previous end
theory_refs.why: How Kadane falls out of the bottleneck method.
What to say when asked why it is correct.
"Best ending at i" is a DP state you will see again on Day 25.

stages.title: Understand
stages.body:
✍️ f(array, possibly negative) → the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
- n ≤ 10⁵ → O(n) or O(n log n).
- [−2,1,−3,4,−1,2,1,−5,4] → 6 ([4,−1,2,1]).

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body:
✍️ By hand: I keep adding while the total helps. When the running total becomes negative it can only drag down anything after it, so I start fresh.
✍️ Hard part: the all-negative case — the answer is the single largest element, not 0.
✍️ Edges: n = 1; all negative; zeros.

stages.title: Brainstorm: brute → optimal
stages.body:
✍️ **1. Brute.** All (i, j), sum each. O(n³), or O(n²) with running sums.
✍️ ↳ Bottleneck: for each end j, trying every start i.
✍️ ↳ Observation: the best subarray ending at j is either [a[j]] alone or (best subarray ending at j−1) + a[j]. So "best ending at j" comes from "best ending at j−1" in O(1).
✍️ **2. Optimal (Kadane).** cur = max(a[j], cur + a[j]); best = max(best, cur). O(n), O(1).
✍️ (Prefix-sum view: answer = max over j of pre[j+1] − min prefix before it — the same as tomorrow's stock problem.)

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body:
✍️ 1. Set cur and best to the first element.
✍️ 2. For each next element: cur becomes the larger of (the element alone) and (cur plus the element).
✍️ 3. Update best with cur.
✍️ 4. Return best.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
STATE   cur = a[0]; best = a[0]
LOOP    for i in 1..n-1
UPDATE    cur  = max(a[i], cur + a[i])     extend or restart
          best = max(best, cur)
RETURN  best
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Edge cases and complexity
stages.body:
✍️ O(n) time, O(1) space.
✍️ All negative [−3, −1, −2] → −1. `best = 0` initialisation would wrongly return 0.

stages.title: Carry forward
stages.body:
✍️ "Best contiguous segment" → state = best ending exactly here; extend or restart.
✍️ This is the first DP of the plan: dp[i] depends only on dp[i−1].
✍️ Initialise optimisation answers with the first real candidate, not with 0.

stages.title: Interview follow-ups
stages.body:
- *Return the subarray.* Track the start index at each restart and the best (start, end).
- *Divide and conquer version* (LeetCode's follow-up): best of left half, right half, and crossing the middle → O(n log n).
- *Circular array.* max(Kadane, total − min subarray), unless all negative ([[kad-kadane#variations]]).
- *Maximum product.* Track max and min ([[kad-max-product-variant]]).

siblings.title: Maximum Product Subarray
siblings.maps: Kadane with products — but a negative turns the minimum into the maximum, so track both.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body:
✍️ Largest product of a contiguous subarray; values in [−10, 10] including 0.
✍️ Why plain Kadane fails: [−2, 3, −4] → the best is the whole array (24), built from a very negative product times −4.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Keep hi and lo = max and min product ending here. For x < 0 swap them first; then hi = max(x, hi·x), lo = min(x, lo·x). O(n).

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ For each x: if negative, swap hi/lo; update both from the old values; best = max(best, hi).

stages.title: Pseudocode
Reference Java
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ When an operation can flip order (negatives, multiplication), keep both extremes ([[kad-max-product-variant#idea]]).

siblings.title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
siblings.maps: A wrapping subarray = total minus a middle subarray → max(Kadane max, total − Kadane min).

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Max subarray sum when the array is circular (a subarray may wrap from the end to the start).

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Either the best subarray does not wrap (normal Kadane) or it wraps, in which case the excluded part is a contiguous middle block with minimum sum. If every value is negative, the wrap case would be empty → use normal Kadane.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Run max-Kadane and min-Kadane together with the total; answer as above.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
compute maxSub, minSub, total
if maxSub < 0: return maxSub
return max(maxSub, total - minSub)
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ Complement trick: "maximum wrapping part" = "total − minimum non-wrapping part".

siblings.title: Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray
siblings.maps: Run Kadane for the max and for the min; the answer is the bigger magnitude.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Maximum of |sum| over all subarrays (empty allowed → at least 0).

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ |sum| is largest either at the max subarray sum or at the min subarray sum → two Kadanes in one pass.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Track max-ending-here (floored at 0) and min-ending-here (capped at 0); answer = max(best max, −best min).

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
hi = lo = 0; ans = 0
for x: hi = max(0, hi + x); lo = min(0, lo + x); ans = max(ans, hi, -lo)
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ Allowing an empty subarray lets you floor the running value at 0 (classic Kadane variant).
